documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

38 y/o woman transferring primary care. Works as an administrative assistant. Here to establish and for a
physical. Brought her bottles.

Bipolar disorder: diagnosed in early adulthood, on lithium for many years. Sees her psychiatrist every few
months and wants to keep that arrangement. Mood has been steady for years. Psychiatry would like levels drawn here every 6 months if we are willing, results faxed to them.
Agreed.

Migraine: has had them since her teens. Currently a couple a month.
Sumatriptan 100 mg works within an hour; rarely needs the second dose. No daily headache.

Raynaud: fingers go white then blue in the cold since her twenties. Seen by a rheumatologist about once a year.
Gloves, hand warmers, avoids the freezer aisle. No ulcers. Not on anything for it.

PMH: as above. PSH: tonsillectomy as a child.
Meds: lithium carbonate 300 mg BID (psychiatry); sumatriptan 100 mg PRN, max 200 mg/day.
Allergies: NKDA.
FHx: mother with bipolar disorder. Sister with migraines. Maternal grandmother hypothyroid.
SHx: never smoker, no alcohol, no drugs. Lives in Holyoke. Office job.

ROS: no chest pain, dyspnea, palpitations. No rash. No joint swelling. Periods regular.

Exam: well-appearing, pleasant, good eye contact. HEENT normal, tonsils surgically absent. Thyroid not enlarged,
no nodules. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Hands warm today, normal color, no digital
ulcers or pitting, capillary refill brisk. No tremor. Neuro nonfocal. Skin clear.

PHQ-9: 3.

A/P
1. Bipolar disorder, stable on lithium. Lithium level, CMP, TSH today; repeat every 6 months and copy to
   psychiatry.
2. Migraine, episodic. Continue sumatriptan; will take over refills.
3. Raynaud phenomenon. Continue cold measures, rheum follows.
4. Health maintenance: CBC, lipids, HIV and hep C screen today. Last Pap 2016 at prior office per pt; records
   requested. Mammogram discussion at 40.

documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT PSYCHIATRY — LETTER TO PRIMARY CARE
Date of visit: 10/07/2020

Dear colleague,

I saw Ms. Brooks, 42, for her scheduled follow-up of bipolar disorder. She has remained stable on lithium
throughout the past two years, takes it reliably, and reports no manic or depressive episodes. She had no
concerns of her own today, though on questioning she mentioned that she has been thirstier and urinating more
than usual over the last few weeks. Mental status and a brief physical examination were unremarkable.

Labs drawn here today:
  Sodium 142 mEq/L | Potassium 4.1 mEq/L | Creatinine 1.0 mg/dL | Calcium 10.2 mg/dL
  Lithium 1.2 mEq/L (therapeutic 0.6-1.2)
  TSH 5.5 uIU/mL (ref 0.4-4.0)

Impression: bipolar disorder, stable. Lithium-associated (drug-induced) hypothyroidism, mild, with a TSH just
above range.

Plan: continue lithium carbonate 300 mg twice daily. No thyroid replacement at this level; I would ask that you
repeat a TSH with free T4 in 6 to 8 weeks along with her usual lithium level and renal panel. I will see her
again in 3 months.

Current medications: lithium carbonate 300 mg BID; sumatriptan 100 mg PRN. Allergies: NKDA.

Outpatient psychiatry

documents.body:
RHEUMATOLOGY — FOLLOW-UP NOTE (received by fax 06/07/2021)
Date of service: 04/14/2021

Patient: Erin Brooks, 42-year-old woman with bipolar disorder on lithium and long-standing Raynaud
phenomenon, seen in continuing follow-up.

Interval: After a winter of more frequent vasospastic attacks she called us, and amlodipine 5 mg daily was
started by phone on 04/09. Five days in, she already has fewer attacks. She has noticed her heartbeat even at
rest and occasional facial flushing. No chest pain, dizziness or leg swelling. Migraine history noted; no recent
attack.

Medications: lithium carbonate 300 mg BID, sumatriptan 100 mg PRN (max 200 mg/day), amlodipine 5 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: Vital signs stable. Heart without murmur, rub or gallop. Lungs clear without crackles or wheeze.
Extremities warm, peripheral pulses good, capillary refill brisk, no edema.

ECG (baseline, today): normal.

Assessment: Chronic vasospastic disorder — her Raynaud phenomenon — improving on a dihydropyridine calcium
channel blocker. Palpitations and flushing are expected effects of this class and do not warrant stopping.

Plan: continue amlodipine 5 mg daily. Cold protection as before. Return in 12 months or sooner if attacks
worsen or digital ulcers appear.

Rheumatology

documents.title: Gastroenterology consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
GASTROENTEROLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of service: 04/18/2022
Referred by: primary care

Reason: two weeks of loose stools.

History: Ms. Brooks is a 43-year-old woman with bipolar disorder, migraine and Raynaud phenomenon. She reports
two weeks of 4 to 5 watery bowel movements a day, without blood or mucus. No abdominal pain, weight loss,
travel, sick contacts, known food allergies or change in diet. When asked specifically about supplements, she
told us that about three weeks ago, after reading about natural treatments for migraine, she started a
magnesium oxide 400 mg capsule each night at bedtime.

Medications: lithium carbonate 300 mg BID; sumatriptan 100 mg PRN (max 200 mg/day); amlodipine 5 mg daily.
Supplement: magnesium oxide 400 mg at bedtime (self-started).
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol, administrative assistant.

Exam: vital signs within normal limits. Abdomen soft and nontender, bowel sounds increased. No masses.

Studies: CBC, electrolytes and TSH normal. Stool culture, ova and parasites and fecal leukocytes negative.

Impression: osmotic diarrhea from magnesium oxide.

Plan: stop the magnesium oxide; stools should normalize within days. Colonoscopy is not indicated at her age
without red flags. Please contact us if diarrhea persists beyond two weeks off magnesium.

Gastroenterology

rest, mostly early in the morning before she gets up, sometimes waking her. Each lasts about 15 minutes and goes
away on its own. Not brought on by walking or stairs. No sweating, nausea, or shortness of breath with them. No
palpitations. Nothing today. Has not tried anything for them.

Meds: lithium carbonate 300 mg BID; amlodipine 5 mg daily; sumatriptan 100 mg PRN. NKDA.
Never smoker.

Exam: comfortable. Heart regular, no murmur, rub or gallop. Lungs clear. Chest wall not tender. No edema.

ECG in office: normal sinus rhythm, no ST changes.

A/P: Episodic rest chest discomfort, early morning, self-limited, normal resting ECG. Not typical of exertional
angina; reflux or musculoskeletal less likely given the timing and quality. Would like cardiology to see her
soon. Referral placed, front desk to get the first available.
Reviewed: call 911 for chest pain lasting more than 20 minutes, or with fainting or shortness of breath.

During her early-morning appointment she developed a typical episode in clinic. A 12-lead ECG obtained during
the pain showed transient ST-segment elevation, which resolved with the symptom.

Labs: troponin I within normal limits. Triglycerides 100 mg/dL.

Assessment: Vasospastic (variant) angina.

Plan:

documents.title: Endocrinology consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
ENDOCRINOLOGY — NEW CONSULTATION AND RESULTS
Date of visit: 10/13/2025; results discussed by phone 10/17/2025
Referred by: walk-in clinic (urgent)

HPI: Ms. Brooks is a 47-year-old woman with bipolar disorder on long-term lithium and a prior episode of
lithium-related hypothyroidism, who comes with ongoing thirst. She drinks roughly 4 to 5 liters of water daily
and is often up at night to void. Sleep is poor. She has lost about 5 pounds while eating normally and feels
heat intolerant.

PMH: bipolar disorder; migraine; Raynaud phenomenon; vasospastic angina; prior drug-induced hypothyroidism.
PSH: tonsillectomy in childhood.
Medications (per list we were sent / patient): lithium carbonate 300 mg BID; sumatriptan 100 mg PRN (max
200 mg/day); amlodipine 5 mg daily; magnesium oxide 400 mg at bedtime.
Allergies: NKDA.
FHx: mother bipolar disorder; sister migraine; maternal grandmother hypothyroidism.
SHx: administrative assistant; never smoker; no alcohol.

Exam: vital signs within normal limits; weight 62.6 kg, height 165 cm, BMI 23. Fine tremor of the hands. Mild
lid lag. Thyroid neither enlarged nor tender.

Data: walk-in clinic labs 10/06: TSH 0.06, free T4 2.4, sodium 145, creatinine 1.0, lithium 0.9.
Ours 10/13: TSH receptor antibody negative. TPO antibody 12 IU/mL. Serum osmolality 296, urine osmolality
145 mOsm/kg.
Thyroid ultrasound 10/16: normal size, no nodules, vascularity not increased.

Assessment:
1. Lithium-induced painless thyroiditis, thyrotoxic phase. Antibody negative, normal-sized gland without
   increased flow; not Graves.
2. Lithium-induced nephrogenic diabetes insipidus: polyuria with dilute urine and high-normal serum sodium and
   osmolality.

Plan:
- Thyroiditis: expected to settle over weeks to months. We are deliberately not using a beta blocker given her
  vasospastic angina and Raynaud. Repeat TSH and free T4 in about 6 weeks.
- NDI: amiloride 5 mg daily started 10/17. Discussed with her psychiatrist, who prefers to continue lithium
  given years of stability; we agree. Please check BMP and lithium level one week after starting.
- Free access to water; she should not restrict fluids, and should seek care if unable to drink.
- Return 6 weeks.

Endocrinology
